record.original_question: f (z) meromorphic in D, f ′ (z)f (z)n 6= 1, for n ≥ 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the open unit disc, and let $n\ge 3$ be an integer. Consider the family
$$\mathcal{F} = \{\, f : f \text{ is meromorphic on } D \text{ and } f'(z)\,f(z)^n \neq 1 \text{ for every } z\in D\,\}.$$
Prove or disprove: the family $\mathcal{F}$ is normal on $D$ (in the sense of Montel, with respect to the spherical metric); that is, every sequence in $\mathcal{F}$ has a subsequence which converges locally uniformly on $D$ to a meromorphic function or to the constant $\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: The normality version of Hayman's conjecture — that a family of meromorphic functions on the unit disc with $f'f^n\neq 1$ is normal — has been established for $n\ge 3$ (and indeed extended to smaller $n$ in subsequent work) via the Pang–Zalcman rescaling lemma and related results. It is reported as a confirmed theorem in standard references on normal families and in survey/contribution papers on Hayman's work.

status_evidence.title: Hayman's contribution to the theory of meromorphic functions (Eremenko)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of Hayman's conjectures, including the normal-family version that f'f^n ≠ 1 implies normality for n ≥ 3, later refined to smaller n.
status_evidence.claim: The Hayman normality conjecture for n ≥ 3 has been proven.

status_evidence.title: Some Notes on Normality Criteria of Meromorphic Functions
status_evidence.snippet: States the theorem confirming Hayman's conjecture: if F is a family of meromorphic functions in D with f' - af^n ≠ b for n ≥ 3, then F is normal in D.
status_evidence.claim: Theorem confirming the normality criterion for n ≥ 3 is established in the literature.
